html:
Burma, officially Myanmar since 1989, is the country on the Irrawaddy river in the west of mainland Southeast Asia. The map shows it in 1815 and from 1945 to 2010.

In 1815 it was the kingdom of the Konbaung dynasty (Taungoo and Konbaung Burma) at its largest. It had taken Arakan (Mrauk U) in 1785 and then Manipur and Assam, which brought it up against British India. Three Anglo Burmese wars, in 1824, 1852 and 1885, ended with the whole country under Britain, ruled as a province of India until 1937.

Japan occupied Burma in the Second World War. The nationalist leader Aung San won a promise of independence but was murdered in 1947, months before it came in January 1948. Wars with ethnic minorities started at once and have never fully ended. The army seized power in 1962 and ran the country for decades. It crushed the 8888 Uprising and kept Aung San Suu Kyi under house arrest for years. Cyclone Nargis killed well over 100,000 people in 2008. A partial opening after 2010 ended with the Rohingya exodus in 2017 and a new coup in 2021.
